        Generated for scope 'lab'. Verified on a lab unit (8.10, 2026-10-12). It is the unit's whole IP Tables list, in the
        unit's order, from the scope's management permit list (tacctl scope mgmt-acl lab list; the global
        tacctl config mgmt-acl list when the scope has none), the tacctl server's address and the scope's
        SNMP clients (tacctl scope snmp lab clients list). Add one line per entry under /N, IP Tables,
        in this order. The number is the line's place in the list, not part of the command; a line that
        starts with # is a note for you. The final DROP is not in this list: it is the last step, below.

             # the unit's own traffic: loopback, and the replies to its own connections
          1. iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
          2. iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
             # the tacctl server 10.0.0.42/32: ssh
          3. iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
             # no entry of the management permit list for scope 'lab' permits ssh (tcp/22): only the tacctl server is permitted for ssh
             # permitted range 192.0.2.0/24: udp/161, icmp
          4. iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
          5. iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
             # SNMP (udp 161): the tacctl server, then the scope's SNMP clients
          6. iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
             # ICMP (ping) from the same networks, on eth0
          7. iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.42/32 -p icmp -j ACCEPT

        The same rules in one paste, for the IP Tables prompt (/N, item 5): no comments, no DROP. The paste
        replaces every entry the unit holds, so read its list first ('>' and '<' page through it): what this
        list lacks is gone afterwards. The unit takes the block in one go ("Configuring iptables - Please
        wait..."), applies the rules at once and shows 'IP Tables: On' on the /N menu; any session that
        leaves a top-level menu saves the configuration, this paste included. The block is at the left
        margin on purpose: paste it as it is.

<iptables>
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 192.0.2.0/24 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.0/24 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p udp -s 10.0.0.42/32 --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.42/32 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
</iptables>

        Notes on the list:
          - Line 2: older builds take '-m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED' in place of
            '-m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED'. It covers the replies of the unit's own TACACS+,
            RADIUS, DNS and NTP queries.
          - A permitted range may reach what its entry lists: ssh (tcp/22) and the other services as
            written, or every protocol and port when the entry is plain. Telnet, http and https are not
            permitted unless an entry lists them (tacctl scope mgmt-acl lab add <cidr>:tcp/22,tcp/443) or is
            plain.
          - The udp 161 lines are the SNMP client restriction of Step 6, unless the unit has an SNMP
            access menu of its own (then enter the same clients there).
          - ICMP (ping): the last lines accept it from the same networks, on eth0 only. The unit's own
            'Ping Access' item (/N, item 30; Limited by default) is separate and not changed by this list.
          - A network whose entry is plain or lists icmp has no ICMP line of its own in the last lines (its
            entry covers it).
          - IPv4 only: the unit's 'iptables', not 'ip6tables'. An IPv6 entry of the lists is skipped, with a note.
          - The unit holds 48 entries (12 to a page): this list has 7; with the DROP, the
            OUTPUT ACCEPT and the three policies of the last step, 12. A command is 256 characters at most.

        # iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
        NOT rendered as a paste: no entry of the management permit list of scope 'lab' (tacctl scope mgmt-acl lab list)
        permits ssh (tcp/22), so the DROP would lock out every administrator but the tacctl server. Add the
        permitted ranges with ssh (tacctl scope mgmt-acl lab add <cidr> or <cidr>:tcp/22), then run this command again.
        The walkthrough applies no DROP in any case; the list above is safe to paste without one.
